correctness.rationale: The rational-canonical classification partitions commuting base pairs into joint-centralizer dimensions 3, 5 and 9 with exact counts V,U,\(q^2\). Nondegenerate matrix trace duality yields tangent dimension 9+d. Smooth fibers lift in \(q^{24}\) ways; scalar bases reduce to unrestricted first-order commuting pairs, contributing \(q^{18}T\). At nonscalar rank-one-shift bases the five-dimensional centralizer D has two-dimensional center and all other internal commutator maps have rank two, in both semisimple and nilpotent rank-one cases and all characteristics. The second-order obstruction yields exactly \(q^{23}(q^3+q^2-1)\) lifts. Standalone finite-field checker passed over q=2,3,4,5 including extension field and exhaustive characteristic-two obstruction tests.

originality.rationale: The distinct contribution is the exact degree-two \(\mathbb F_q\) arithmetic lift count over \(\mathbb F_q[t]/(t^3)\) and its rank-two obstruction classification in all characteristics. Prior geometric irreducibility (Sethuraman–Šivic), base joint-centralizer branching (Sharma), and characteristic-zero irregular loci (Popov) substantially overlap but do not logically deliver the displayed second-jet fiber counts. A possibly implicit earlier equivalent local-ring enumeration remains a significant priority risk.
residual_risks: Full historical search of arbitrary finite local ring commuting-matrix enumeration is not exhaustive; implicit equivalent formula may exist.

value.rationale: The second-order jet count is a natural arithmetic invariant of the classical commuting-matrix scheme. Its complete point-count and per-base fiber census distinguish smooth regular, rank-one irregular and scalar loci, quantify infinitesimal arithmetic thickness invisible to irreducibility alone, and hold over every finite field without excluding small characteristics.
